S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
examples: Starts homework or projects but fails to complete them, submitting unfinished work or missing deadlines.
When given multi-step instructions, follows only the first few steps and forgets the rest.
Starts cleaning or organizing but switches to another task midway, failing to finish.
Leaves almost completed work reports or paperwork unfinished, neglecting the final steps.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
examples: Frequently loses school supplies or office supplies like pens, erasers, and calculators.
Always searching for glasses, cell phones, wallets, or keys because they do not know where they are.
Loses necessary documents or materials at home or in the office and cannot find them.
Cannot remember where they placed an item they were holding just moments ago.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
examples: Raises hand or blurts out the answer before the question is even finished in class or meetings.
Jumps to conclusions and speaks before the other person finishes their sentence.
Answers hastily without reading the question to the end in quizzes or exams.
Interrupts and answers in the middle of a conversation without listening to the other person until the end.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), Combined Presentation, is characterized by a persistent pattern of both inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning or development across multiple settings (e.g., home, school, work). Symptoms begin in childhood, though many individuals are not diagnosed until adolescence or adulthood, especially if they have developed compensatory strategies or chosen environments that partly mask their difficulties. The course tends to be chronic, with hyperactive behaviors often becoming more internalized (e.g., restlessness) over time, while inattention and disorganization frequently remain prominent and impairing. ADHD is distinguished from anxiety, mood, and personality disorders by its early onset, cross-situational pattern, and core deficits in sustained attention, executive functioning, and impulse control rather than primarily affective or situational triggers.

patient.stressor: Over the past several years of retirement, Antonio’s loosely structured days had suited his lifelong tendency to jump between gardening, painting, cooking experiments, and community storytelling without much formal planning. About 14 months ago, his wife developed mobility issues after a minor stroke, and Antonio took on managing her appointments, medications, and insurance paperwork in addition to coordinating the neighborhood garden and youth storytelling projects. The increased load of schedules, forms, and follow-through exposed longstanding but previously manageable organizational difficulties, leading to repeated missed appointments, double-booked commitments, and mounting tension at home when his wife felt she could not rely on him for practical tasks despite his obvious devotion. After a frustrated primary care visit where Antonio admitted he felt "scattered" and overwhelmed by basic daily responsibilities despite being otherwise physically well, his doctor referred him for a psychiatric evaluation to explore attention and planning problems that had become clearly impairing in his caregiving and community roles.
patient.chief_complaint: I keep forgetting everyday things like appointments and errands, and it’s starting to really mess up taking care of my wife and my commitments in the garden project.

S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
S001.manifestation: When I’m filling out the online forms for my wife’s insurance or the sign-up sheets for the garden project, I’ll swear I’ve done them carefully, but then I find out I skipped whole sections or typed the wrong date or medication dose because my eyes just kind of jumped over the small print.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
S004.manifestation: I’ll start out meaning to sort my wife’s pills for the week or finish a new story for the kids’ group, but halfway through I wander off to stir a sauce or check on the tomatoes and then realize hours later that I never actually finished the first thing.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
S007.manifestation: I’m constantly hunting for my glasses, the little notebook with all the appointment times, or the folder with the insurance papers, even though I just had them in my hand a minute before and put them down “somewhere safe” that I can’t remember.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
S008.manifestation: When I try to sit down and call the hospital or go over the mail, the slightest thing—a bird at the feeder, the TV in the other room, or a thought about a recipe I want to try—pulls my mind away, and five minutes later I’m doing something else and the papers are still untouched.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
S009.manifestation: Lately I’ll tell myself, “Remember, you have to call the physio at three and pick up her prescription after,” and then I get busy with the garden or talking to a neighbor and only realize I’ve completely forgotten until my wife asks me hours later what happened.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: If I have to sit in the waiting room at the clinic or stay beside my wife while she watches her shows, I feel this jumpy energy in my body, like I need to get up and move or fiddle with something, and I keep shifting in my seat and looking for excuses to stand up.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: Even when I try to relax with one of my old hobbies, like reading or painting quietly, I end up talking to myself, humming, getting up to check on something in the kitchen, or turning on the radio because just sitting there calmly in silence makes me antsy.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
S014.manifestation: From the moment I wake up, I’m bouncing between making breakfast, checking the garden, tidying the living room, and sorting mail so much that my daughter jokes I never stop moving, but I still don’t feel like I actually finish much of anything.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
S016.manifestation: In meetings with the garden committee or when the doctor is explaining something, I find myself jumping in with what I think they’re going to say or answering before they finish the question, and then I realize I’ve cut them off or missed an important detail.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
S017.manifestation: When I’m in line at the pharmacy or waiting for our turn at the clinic, I get impatient and fidgety, checking the time over and over, muttering about how long it’s taking, and sometimes I edge forward or try to ask the staff questions before it’s really my turn.

add_requirements.onset_prior_to_12_years: Even back in primary school, my teachers were always telling my parents that I couldn’t sit still, was constantly talking out of turn, and left half-finished worksheets on my desk because I’d lose track of what we were supposed to be doing.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: These days my forgetfulness and jumping between tasks mean my wife sometimes misses or is late to appointments, our bills and insurance forms get messed up, and I’ve had to back out of parts of the garden and storytelling projects because people feel they can’t count on me to follow through.
add_requirements.duration: The way these attention and restlessness problems have really started to interfere with caring for my wife and keeping up with all the paperwork has been going on for a little over a year, ever since her stroke and my taking over her care.
